name: Lyft, Inc

events.what: CFO appointed (Erin Brewer retiring, advisor to 2026-12-15)
events.from: Lyft insider for nearly eight years (Head of Lyft Urban Solutions, Head of Strategy and Growth, Head of FP&A)

events.what: Co-founders Logan Green and John Zimmer left the board; Sean Aggarwal named Chair; board cut 9 to 7

events.from: ex Waymo Chief Safety Officer, ex NTSB Chair

events.what: Acquisition of Freenow (European taxi app), EUR 204.1M ($234.8M); TBR Global Chauffeuring also acquired in 2025 (terms not verified)

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Lyft's target is adjusted EBITDA as a percent of GROSS BOOKINGS (about 4% in 2027, from about 2.1% targeted for 2024), not of revenue. Consensus margins in this record (FY2026 to FY2028, and the grid's 10.7%) are EBITDA over REVENUE. Gap math uses the gross bookings basis: consensus FY2027 EBITDA ($894M, data_financials 2026-10-01) over consensus FY2027 gross bookings ($24.76B, VA company data fetched 2026-08-29). Translated to a revenue basis, 4% of consensus gross bookings is 11.88% of consensus revenue versus 10.73% modeled (about 115 bps), but that is a basis translation, not the stated target.

statements.quote: By 2027, we expect to reach adjusted EBITDA margin as a percentage of gross bookings of approximately 4% on a full-year basis, driven by the pillars of our customer-obsessed strategy.
statements.speaker: Erin Brewer

statements.quote: Importantly, we expect that conversion of Adjusted EBITDA to Free Cash Flow will grow from at least 70% in 2024 to more than 90% from 2025 to 2027, driven by our growing profitability, our asset-light model, and contributions from working capital, supported by the progress in our insurance strategy.
statements.speaker: Erin Brewer

statements.quote: When you put that all together, we expect that in 2027, Lyft will grow to a company with approximately $25 billion in gross bookings, approximately $1 billion in adjusted EBITDA, and generate over $900 million in free cash flow.
statements.speaker: Erin Brewer

statements.quote: We did all this and more while tracking relentlessly towards our 2027 goals we outlined at our Investor Day back in 2024. That's $25 billion in Gross Bookings, 4% Adjusted EBITDA margin, and Free Cash Flow of over $1 billion.
statements.speaker: David Risher

statements.quote: As I think about the targets we set out for 2027, right? We talked about our goals around top-line growth. We said steady margin expansion and, of course, Free Cash Flow. So the components of margin expansion remain the same as we outlined at Investor Day.
statements.speaker: Erin Brewer

street.gap_assumption: Gross bookings basis on both sides: 4.0% target versus consensus FY2027 EBITDA / consensus FY2027 gross bookings = 3.61%. consensus_ebitda_margin_by_fy is EBITDA / revenue and is not comparable to the target. Consensus FY2027 gross bookings $24.76B versus about $25B target; consensus EBITDA $894M versus about $1B target.
street.source: Baba data_financials consensus (Visible Alpha) plus data_company_data gross bookings

evidence_of_progress.note: Order [Q1 2026, Q2 2026], adj. EBITDA as % of gross bookings. Q1 2.7% vs 2.6% (+13 bps computed, $132.8M on $4,946.0M vs $106.5M on $4,162.4M); Q2 3.2% vs 2.9% (+34 bps computed, $177.2M on $5,504.2M vs $129.4M on $4,490.1M), 8-K EX-99.1 document_id 142981. Q3 2026 guide 3.3% to 3.6%, reconfirmed 2026-09-30 alongside a $272.5M California misclassification settlement (excluded from adj. EBITDA; 8-K 0001628280-26-064095). LTM 2.97% leaves about 100 bps to reach 4% in 2027.

verdict: Partial match: cheap (0th pctile EV/EBITDA, down 39%) with a dated, CEO and CFO repeated 4%-of-gross-bookings 2027 target, but the target is from June 2024, the new CFO is an insider effective 2026-09-28, and consensus already sits at 3.61% of gross bookings for 2027, only 39 bps short.
open_questions: Will Michael Brous restate the 2027 framework (now including Freenow and TBR) or set a new long-range plan with the Q3 2026 print in November?
Can the margin jump from 2.97% LTM to about 4% in 2027 when the last two quarters expanded only 13 and 34 bps year over year?
Does the AV transition (Waymo depot in Nashville, AV partnerships) add cost that pushes the 4% beyond 2027?
